title: The Hour Bank
logline: At Kevin's first party with the gang, Marshall corners him by the dip with his oldest theory: the hour that vanishes every March is being stolen. Kevin, the most rational man Robin has ever dated, realizes his therapy hour is only fifty minutes, and within a week he's planning a rooftop stakeout with a net. Ted, Lily and Barney each try to deprogram him and each makes it worse, while Marshall starts to worry that his first believer is a better truther than he is.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2012, your Aunt Robin was dating the calmest, most reasonable man in New York. Then he spent ten minutes in our kitchen with your Uncle Marshall.

couch.line: Bigfoot was just the gateway theory.

scenes.summary: Kevin's first party with the gang. Robin gives him rules, the top one being: never get stuck in the kitchen with Marshall. Barney answers 'Please' to what he does. Marshall pitches the Hour Bank; Kevin validates politely, asks for evidence, and Marshall asks where the other ten minutes of a therapy hour go. Kevin says 'Huh.' Robin panics. Button: Kevin asks for literature.

beats.line: It was the first time Aunt Robin brought Kevin to one of our parties.
Ground rules. Don't let Barney teach you a handshake. It has nine parts, and one of them is a lie.
Don't tell Lily anything about your childhood. She will use it.
Hi, Kevin! Was your mom a hugger?
And whatever you do, never get stuck in the kitchen with Marshall.
Robin, I sit with people in crisis for a living. I think I can handle a man by the guacamole.
He has been waiting by that guacamole for a man like you his whole life.
Kevin! Barney. Big fan of your work. Robin's been way less stabby.
Thanks. So, Barney, what do you do?
Please.
Interesting. Most people just answer that.
Most people have jobs you can say out loud.
I followed him to work once. He walked into a revolving door and never came out the other side.
Kevin! Buddy! Come try my seven-layer dip. It's only got six layers, and I have a theory.
Don't go.
Robin. It's a dip.
Kevin. What happens every March at two in the morning?
Daylight saving time. The clocks spring forward.
From one fifty-nine straight to three. An entire hour. Gone.
Three hundred million Americans lose an hour of their lives, and nobody files a police report?
It comes back in November.
Does it, Kevin? Or do they give you back a different one?
In November you get one AM twice. That's not your hour, Kevin. That's a used hour with a stain on it.
Oh no. He's doing the Hour Bank.
Relax. Kevin's a pro. He'll nod, he'll validate, he'll leave.
It sounds like this hour is really important to you.
Kevin. Nobody has ever validated my hour before.
Lily loves me. But whenever I bring up the Hour Bank, she does the nod.
Mm-hm.
And who runs this Hour Bank?
Nobody knows. But somewhere out there is a man who's had three hundred extra years of Sundays.
Marshall, I appreciate you sharing. But as a professional, I'd need some evidence.
Okay. You're a therapist. How long is a therapy hour?
Fifty minutes. It's the industry standard.
Kevin. Where do the other ten minutes go?
Paperwork. Everybody uses them for paperwork.
Do you do paperwork in those ten minutes?
I mostly eat almonds.
Huh.
No. No, no, no. He said huh.
Huh is how it starts. That's how I got into Gothic Revival.
Marshall. Do you have any literature?
Lily! He wants literature!
Kids, Marshall printed those pamphlets in 2004. Kevin got the first one. Lily got the rest, as coasters.

scenes.summary: Six days later at Marshall's law firm. Kevin has gone through twelve years of appointment books, given every patient the full sixty in protest, drawn a pie chart of suspects and wants a rooftop stakeout with forty clocks and a net. Marshall is thrilled, then unnerved. Kevin converts Arthur Hobbs in four questions. Robin arrives: she said 'I love you' and Kevin checked his watch. She'll call in the others; Marshall agrees, a little sadly. Button: Arthur wants the brief in forty real minutes.

beats.line: Six days later, Kevin dropped by Marshall's office. He brought his own markers.
Marshall. I've been up since four. Technically three, if they'd let me keep it.
Kevin! Look at you! You've got the eyes! The two in the morning eyes!
Twelve years of fifty-minute sessions. That's three thousand hours. Gone. From my patients. On my watch.
So this week, everybody got the full sixty. In protest.
Mister Dworsky finally cried about his father. Minute fifty-four. He'd been six minutes away for nine years.
Twenty years I've been the only guy in the room. Now there's two of us!
Four suspects. Ranked by motive.
beats.title: Where Does The Hour Go?

beats.line: Brunch. It steals from breakfast and lunch, and it only happens on Sundays!
Saturday, two AM, your roof. I'm bringing forty synchronized clocks, two cameras, a thermos and a net.
A net? Kevin, what are we catching?
The hour, Marshall.
Buddy, nobody catches it. That's not what the roof is for.
Then what is the roof for?
Snacks? Talking about it? It's mostly snacks.
Marshall. You were right. Don't you dare go soft on me now.
Eriksen! Who is this man, and why is he drawing pie on my whiteboard?
Mister Hobbs, this is Kevin. He's a therapist.
I don't need a therapist. I need the Hendricks brief in forty minutes.
Mister Hobbs. How long is your lunch hour?
Forty minutes. I'm not a monster.
Then who took the other twenty?
Legal.
I walk Tugboat for an hour every night. He comes home so tired, Kevin. Is it an hour?
Saturday. Two AM. Bring the dog.
Walk me to the elevator. I have questions about Switzerland.
Marshall. Why did my boyfriend just get into an elevator with your boss, talking about Switzerland?
I've dated a ventriloquist, a guy with eleven ferrets, and Barney. Kevin was supposed to be the sane one.
Last night, for the first time in my life, I told a man I loved him.
Robin!
He checked his watch and said, is it, though? Is it really eleven forty?
I'm calling Ted, Lily and Barney. We're deprogramming him before Saturday.
But if you deprogram him, he won't come up to the roof with me.
That's the idea.
Right. Yeah. Good idea.
Eriksen. The Hendricks brief. Forty minutes.
Real minutes.

scenes.summary: Friday night intervention while Marshall is out. Kevin explains why he fell for it: nobody ever asks what he thinks. Ted's slideshow on the Day of Two Noons makes Ted say huh. Lily's kindergarten time-out ends with Lily afraid of the cable company. Barney confesses to being the Hour Bank so Kevin can 'win', and 'Please' becomes proof. Kevin summons Barney to the handoff. Button: Lily on the cable company.

beats.line: Friday night, the night before the clocks changed, we held an intervention.
He's on his way up. Remember, he's a trained professional. He'll see right through you.
Robin, I once talked a mime into talking. I can talk a therapist out of a clock.
Kevin, we love you. This is an intervention.
Robin, I've run forty interventions. You never open with, this is an intervention.
You're the most rational man I've ever met. What happened?
Twelve years of asking people how that made them feel. Nobody ever asks what I think.
Marshall asked. And I think it's a heist.
Kevin, I'm going to dismantle this the way I dismantle everything. With a slideshow.
Slide one of thirty-one.
beats.title: The Day of Two Noons
lines: New York clocks set back four minutes

beats.line: And where did the extra four minutes come from, Ted?
From the railroads.
And where did the railroads get them?
Huh.
Ted. Don't you dare huh.
Dad. Did you get converted?
Kids, I was not converted. I was curious. For about nine months.
My turn. When a kindergartner gets a crazy idea stuck in his head, only one thing works.
Kevin, you're in time-out. Five minutes. Think about what you've done.
Five minutes on whose clock, Lily?
My clock.
And who set your clock?
The cable company.
And who sets the cable company's clock?
Robin, I'm scared.
Amateurs. You can't argue a man out of a conspiracy. You give him a villain, and then you let him win.
Kevin. It's me. I'm the Hour Bank.
Go on.
Every March I take one hour from every American. How else would I find time for all of this?
The gym. The tailor. Two dates a night. Eight hours of beauty sleep. Nobody fits that into a normal day.
But it's over. I'm retiring. You beat me, Kevin. Go home.
Barney. What do you do for a living?
Please.
Oh my God.
No, that's just a thing I say when—
If you're really retiring, you'll come to the handoff. Two AM. My girlfriend's roof. Bring the hours.
Is there a handoff?
Great. Now my boyfriend's a truther with a suspect.
Technically, he has a confession.
Thank you, Ted.
And while he's at it, somebody should really look into the cable company.

scenes.summary: The stakeout, 1:40 AM. Robin confiscated the net; Arthur canceled. Marshall confesses he never wanted to catch anything, just to have someone up there with him. Kevin waives Tuesday. Robin arrives to take Kevin home; Kevin's case for believing without evidence is Robin's packed bag. Some gyms are in Canada. The gang arrives; Barney admits he made it up; Lily stops nodding. At 1:59 Barney's phone rings and he steps out. The clock jumps; Lily asks where it went. Barney returns: what'd I miss? Robin's bringing the net next year. Future Ted button.

beats.line: Saturday night, one forty in the morning. Nineteen minutes until the hour disappeared.
Clocks one through forty, synchronized. Camera rolling. Thermos full.
Where's the net?
Robin found the net.
We're not talking right now.
And Mister Hobbs canceled. Tugboat had a bad feeling.
Kevin, buddy. Sit down. I have to tell you something.
I don't want to catch the hour.
Twenty years of Bigfoot, I never once packed a net. What would I even do with him?
He's huge, he's confused, and he doesn't have a lease.
Then what are we doing up here?
This. A roof, a cooler, and something nobody else believes. With somebody.
Lily nods. Ted footnotes. Barney charges a cover.
Then you asked for literature. Kevin, you're the first person who ever stayed for the whole hour.
Marshall, that's beautiful.
I'm going to waive Tuesday.
Tuesday was a session?
Kevin. It's almost two in the morning. I'm taking you home.
Robin, there's a packed bag by your door. Passport, toothbrush, hockey stick.
And every morning, I believe you're going to stay. Don't tell me I can't believe things without evidence.
Kevin, that bag is for the gym.
It has your passport in it.
Some gyms are in Canada.
Fine. I'm staying. But if anything comes out of the sky, I'm shooting it.
I lay awake all night, Kevin. Where did the railroads get four minutes?
Kevin, for the record, I made the whole thing up. I'm not the Hour Bank.
He's really not. He's not that organized.
I know, Barney. It doesn't matter. We're just here to watch it go.
Thirty seconds!
Marshmallow? I'm not nodding.
Sorry. I have to take this.
Marshall.
I know.
Three. Two. One.
Three o'clock.
Where did it go?
Sorry, guys. What'd I miss?
Same time next year?
Same time next year.
Next year, I'm bringing the net.
Kids, every March since, at one fifty-nine, Uncle Barney's phone rings and he steps away. He comes back at three. He swears he was gone one minute. Technically, he's right.
